{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABb-ryYg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhFh9E0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 44, "title": "Build a standards-based FPGA verification workspace with reference models and waveforms", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL currently focuses on editing synthesizable Verilog/SystemVerilog and running the resulting RTL as browser-generated Wasm. The project vision is broader: **a general-purpose FPGA/RTL design and verification workspace in the browser**. Developers should be able to work with an RTL design, a separately authored reference model, testbench stimuli, a scoreboard, waveforms and debugging in one coherent environment.

The user has approved a **compact dark IDE-style UI concept** (2026-11-02): a project tree on the left; side-by-side RTL and reference-model code editors in the center; verification/test results, scoreboard and execution controls on the right; waveforms, signals and logs below; a restrained top-level Design / Simulation / Verification navigation. This is the target layout, **not a screenshot to fake**.

The implementation must follow the existing [three UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable.**

## Goal

Implement the approved verification-centered workspace so developers can use **standard FPGA development artifacts and tools**—Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL, C++ or Python reference models, SystemVerilog testbenches and established verification patterns—without inventing a proprietary WebRTL verification language or file format.

**SNES is only an example**, not the architecture or the default test case. The same workflow should apply to a generic adder, FIFO, processor, DSP or other arbitrary supported RTL project.

## User experience / layout

- **Top navigation:** WebRTL/project identity and clear **Design**, **Simulation**, **Verification** workspaces. Do not introduce fake or inert **Synthesis**, **Device**, cloud-save, share or account actions merely because they appear in the image; show only existing working features, with a future capability added only when implemented.
- **Left project explorer:** compact hierarchical real files/folders and a relevant run configuration. Existing five bundled examples remain available without multiplying them. Source file editing must support the newly needed `.cpp`, `.py` and `.sv` alongside `.v`, with genuine import/add/rename/remove and clear unsaved/replacement handling. The present flat-`.v` restriction will need deliberate, secure updating.
- **Center editor:** genuinely editable, tabbed source files, including an optional **split RTL + reference-model** view. Reuse source contents; no static code previews. A single editor remains usable on narrow screens, with accessible pane switching.
- **Right verification pane:** actual test inventory, running/passed/failed results, useful mismatch details with **expected vs actual**, and existing Run/Pause/Step/Reset controls. Avoid fabricated results (e.g. mockup's “12/12 passed”) or speculative coverage percentages.
- **Bottom analysis pane:** a functional **VCD waveform** viewer or another standard waveform output supported by existing HDL tools, signal values, logs and diagnostics in tabs/disclosures. Render only real recorded signal data; retain existing browser Debug inspection/history and its limits. Provide an actionable path from a mismatch to RTL debug at the correct known boundary.
- Match the mockup's restrained **dark theme, subtle purple accents, dense but readable panels, compact spacing and clear hierarchy**. Retain current accessibility, keyboard navigation, contrast and responsive layout; a theme override must not force a new design-system dependency.
- Show only context-relevant controls. Avoid duplicating the same configuration in multiple places, unnecessary text, or project-specific jargon in the generic UI.

## Standard verification workflow, not a custom framework

Separate the responsibilities explicitly:

1. **DUT:** the user's HDL under test; continue to compile and simulate real RTL.
2. **Reference model:** independently authored **standard C++ or Python**, executed in a browser-compatible sandbox/worker (C++→Wasm via existing compatible compiler where feasible; Python through a real browser Python runtime such as Pyodide). An independently authored synthesizable SV reference module may also be compared through an RTL simulator.
3. **Testbench/stimulus:** support **SystemVerilog testbenches** where the selected browser-compatible simulator actually supports their language features. Investigate standard cocotb conventions for Python-driven testing; reuse cocotb itself where feasible. **Do not mislabel the Yosys/Slang synthesis frontend as a full event-driven SV/UVM simulator.** Unsupported UVM/classes/timing constructs must be rejected or clearly identified rather than silently simulated incorrectly.
4. **Scoreboard/checking:** run the DUT and reference model against controlled equivalent inputs and compare at an explicitly defined clock boundary or transaction/valid-ready boundary. Account for reset, latency, ordering and independently computed expectations. Use familiar verification patterns and existing standards/APIs; any small host bridge must be transport plumbing, not a new WebRTL-only verification DSL.
5. **Debug:** on a mismatch, preserve the RTL state where possible, capture the inputs/observations and give the user a reliable route to inspect signals or reproduce from the recorded test sequence. Do not claim arbitrary backward restore or functional-model→RTL state migration: those are separate compatibility problems.

Start with a **real, generic example** (e.g. counter/adder or small FIFO) proving C++ reference and Python reference can both drive the same DUT and produce meaningful pass/fail evidence. Include at least one real supported **SystemVerilog testbench** example and a deliberately failing case showing an actionable mismatch. Preserve a clean ability to choose only the modules/tools that apply to a particular project.

## Technical boundaries

- Browser-only / static-site deployment remains the normal operating mode: no mandatory server-side compilation, no uploading users' RTL/C++/Python or test artifacts, and strict bounds on source size, worker execution time and memory.
- Existing Verilog/Slang frontend, compiled Fast scheduler with CXXRTL fallback, Debug inspector, Fast↔Debug retained-state handoff, Canvas/Web Audio, SNES and trusted-local functionality must continue to work.
- Different language runtimes may execute independently; synchronize by **explicit observable test events**, not assuming they can share the same heap or flip-flop layout.
- For browser-incompatible cocotb/full SV/UVM workflows, document precise support and limitations. Do not substitute a proprietary near-cocotb API while calling it cocotb, or add a decorative “supported” toggle. Add functionality in coherent increments and leave this Issue open if one of the stated end-to-end requirements is still unmet.
- Keep the implementation testable under the existing **under-10-minute Fast PR CI** with targeted additional verification; do not run the complete SNES cartridge corpus for every UI iteration.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Real, responsive dark IDE-style workspace follows the **project explorer / split source editor / verification results / waveform & diagnostics** composition, with accessible focus/order, error reporting and a usable narrow layout.
- [ ] Create/import/edit/switch/rename/remove real RTL, C++ reference, Python reference and supported SV testbench files without losing edits. The project/file model and HDL compiler receive only appropriate inputs; tool selection is truthful.
- [ ] A real **C++ reference model** runs in the browser and verifies a generic RTL DUT against independently defined expectations.
- [ ] A real **Python reference model** runs in the browser and verifies the same or similarly generic DUT. Compatibility and resource limits are documented.
- [ ] A **SystemVerilog testbench** exercises a DUT through an actually supported simulation frontend, with documented supported language subset. Unsupported advanced testbench/UVM constructs are not presented as working.
- [ ] Testbench/stimulus, reference model and scoreboard roles are clear; demonstrate deterministic PASS and intentionally wrong RTL/reference producing a specific FAIL with expected/actual and the relevant sample/transaction position.
- [ ] A **real standard waveform artifact (prefer VCD)** is generated from sampled RTL activity and displayed or exported; navigation, signal selection and time/cycle labels agree with recorded values.
- [ ] Pause/step, existing RTL Debug inspection and Fast↔Debug state continuity work without spurious reset, and a failed comparison exposes sufficient context for follow-up debugging. Do not claim unsupported time-travel or cross-language state transplant.
- [ ] Existing examples and generic compiler/runtime/media/SNES functionality remain operational. Validate actual browser execution, not screenshot-only DOM or canned rows.
- [ ] Document toolchain provenance/licenses, supported standards/language subsets, browser resource limits and how to run an existing FPGA project/testbench as-is when supported. No new proprietary project file format or verification syntax.
- [ ] Automated browser tests cover end-to-end real model compilation/execution, positive/negative comparison, actual waveform values, file editing, wide/narrow layout, invalid inputs and cancellation/failure cleanup. No human-only design approval gate.

## Implementation guidance

This is an **integrated product milestone** spanning UI and verification runtime; implementation may proceed in reviewed, small PRs (e.g. workspace/file model → C++/Python runner → supported SV testbench → scoreboard/waveform integration). Keep the Issue open until the actual claimed capabilities work. Prioritize reuse of established OSS and standards over building a bespoke verification ecosystem. The user-approved mockup specifies the visual composition, **not** exact file names, fake test data, an SNES-specific project tree or an unsupported Verilator-in-browser claim.

## Verification after merge

After the Pages deployment, run a focused automated public-site smoke that loads a generic RTL+reference project, runs a real comparison, displays the result and a real trace, and verifies ordinary RTL compilation still works. Record the actual deployed result separately; publication is not a pre-merge gate.
